answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it can vote or claim rewards, then slash that stake when an independently verified fraud proof shows the identity coordinated a duplicate claim. One person can still create many keys, but each gains weight only by tying up more capital, and a detected attack destroys some of it. The spiral of repeated registrations therefore compounds the attacker’s exposure; onyx and comet can be harmless names, but neither grants free influence.
